## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One item should be fixed: the README still says the default timeout is 30 seconds, but this PR changes it to 60. The code change itself is correct. `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` feeds the `--timeout` default at `app/cli.py:8`, and an explicit `--timeout` still overrides it. The updated `test_defaults` checks the new value, and the existing `test_explicit_options` covers the override.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- README.md:3 — comments — The README still reads "Requests time out after 30 seconds unless you pass `--timeout SECONDS`." That is no longer true, because this PR sets `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 60` (`app/cli.py:3`) and `parse_args` uses it as the `--timeout` default (`app/cli.py:8`). The diff does not touch README.md, so it now contradicts the code. To fix it, change the README line to say 60 seconds. — Users who rely on the README will expect requests to give up after 30 seconds when they actually wait up to 60. That can lead to wrong tuning of `--timeout` and confusion when they look into slow requests.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- The default stays in the single `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` constant, which `parse_args` uses (`app/cli.py:8`), so the change only needed one line in production code.
- `tests/test_cli.py:8` checks the new default through `parse_args([])`, and `test_explicit_options` (`tests/test_cli.py:13-16`) still shows that an explicit `--timeout 12` overrides it.
